children: Copper futures rebounded from an 11-month low, lifted by gains in technology stocks.

Three-month copper futures on the London Metal Exchange advanced more than 3% in Thursday morning trade, ICE data showed. The gains provided a lift to the broader base metals complex, with LME futures across these contracts trading higher.

Copper prices had declined in recent weeks, pressured by waning sentiment surrounding artificial-intelligence trades. The base metal is critical to data center development and has generally benefited from the artificial-intelligence infrastructure buildout.

Advances in major Asian stock markets on Thursday likely helped underpin copper's gains. Tech-heavy stock indexes such as Hong Kong's Hang Seng Tech and Taiwan's Taiex were up by more than 2% around midday.

Analysts at ANZ Research noted that despite the recent AI stock rout, copper would continue to benefit from the data-center construction boom, as funding for the buildout of data centers is largely in place for the next 18 months.
"In the meantime, traders are still scrambling for available metal across the sector," they said.

The LME three-month copper futures contract jumped as much as 3.8% to $12,089 a metric ton, ICE data showed, before paring gains to trade 2.6% higher. Other base metals also advanced: aluminum gained 1.9%, nickel climbed 2.0%, zinc added 1.95% and tin rose 2.9%.

title: Copper Rebounds From 11-Month Low Amid Tech Stocks Rally
